messages:
alex_f: Ran a quick CPU profile on the ingress host for the streaming path — seeing an unexpected spike in host-side CPU when clients send lots of short streaming tokens (<= 64B). Flamegraph attached (pprof) shows large slice in HTTP/2 frame assembly + our Python tokenizer glue.
maya: ugh. do you have numbers? how big is the delta vs baseline?
alex_f: Baseline (non-streaming) mean CPU/sample ~12ms per request; streaming small-chunk path jumps to ~45ms. Kernel selection/batching work on GPU still fine — this is pre-GPU. Breakdown from perf:
- ~38% syscall/write + http2 framing
- ~25% py tokenizer (tokenizer.py -> encode_loop)
- ~12% msgpack/serialize
- rest is scheduling/idle
cheng_w: can you paste the perf command and pprof link so I can repro locally?
alex_f: perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -p <pid> -- sleep 60
pprof: https://pprof.internal/redwood/ingress/1945001234/stream-host-flame.html
tim_ops: saw similar on a customer env last week. smaller token sizes + high req/s => more gRPC/HTTP2 frames. are we using DATA frames per chunk right now? or coalescing?
alex_f: we currently emit a DATA frame immediately per chunk from the streaming reader. No coalescing. That made sense when chunks were larger. With small chunks it's 3-4x frames per logical token.
sara_ml: is tokenizer running on python worker threadpool? might be GIL causing syscall slowness.
alex_f: tokenizer is python with C-based tokenizer (huggingface/tokenizers) but our glue code decodes/merges prefix metadata in Python, which seems to be the hot path. Also saw lock contention on our stream buffer object.
buildbot: deploy-bot: rollout v2-ingress-patch started at 2025-03-05T17:06:00Z
maya: quick ideas:
- coalesce small DATA frames into a per-request write buffer and flush on threshold/time
- move glue logic into a tiny Rust extension to avoid GIL churn
- batch tokenization for tiny chunks (wait up to 2ms to gather)
- avoid msgpack per-chunk and use a streaming framing format
alex_f: prototyped coalesce in go ingress proxy -> 48% reduction in syscall/write time in local sim. However introduces ~1.2ms p99 add for very low-rate single-client flows. net win for high qps.
cheng_w: can we make coalescing adaptive? e.g., if qps < X bypass, else coalesce, or dynamic coalesce based on observed chunk size distribution.
tim_ops: we should also check HTTP/2 header compression overhead when many small requests use different headers (auth tokens). maybe enable header table size tuning.
sara_ml: for tokenizer glue: moving merge into a rust extension sounds reasonable. small microbench: Python merge loop ~0.8us/op, rust ~0.05us/op (per token metadata merge), so 10-15x.
maya: action items:
- alex: land ingress proxy coalesce toggle behind feature flag and perf test in staging (ETA 2d)
- cheng: prototype adaptive coalesce and metric for "coalesce efficacy" (ETA 4d)
- sara: spike rust glue and bench end-to-end tokenization CPU (ETA 3d)
- tim: check config for HTTP/2 header table and gRPC window sizes across dedicated vs hosted (ETA 1d)
alex_f: logging: added a short repro harness in /infra/tests/ingress/small_chunk_stream.py (run with --qps 200 --chunk-size 32). Put a note in the pprof page with the command.
maya: SGTM. one more thing — KV cache lookups: any correlation? if we hit KV cache for prefix tokens frequently could be adding overhead.
alex_f: good point — KV cache is mostly on the GPU/serving runtime side. but we do a small host-side prefix check to short-circuit; profiler shows ~3% in that code path. will validate.
cheng_w: tagging this with perf/regression for the triage board.
alex_f: FYI I pushed a small opt: don't call msgpack per chunk; reuse preallocated buffer -> 10% end-to-end CPU drop in sim.
maya: nice. keep notes light in the PR. we prefer a small canary rollout and metric dashboard: host cpu, p99 latency, frames/sec, coalesce ratio.
tim_ops: once coalesce flag is ready, I'll run it in dedicated region A for 6h. if p99 increases >1.5ms rollback.
sara_ml: I'll share microbench results in #eng-ml after the rust spike.
alex_f: thanks all. next sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow 11:00 to decide canary plan. :thumbsup:
maya: :raised_hands:
